title: Field Pilot Ops Manifest and Observability Checklist
summary: Operational playbook for a customer field pilot: rollout cadence, responsibilities, lightweight risk register, and an observability checklist to validate production readiness during a 3-week POC.
body:
Purpose:
- Provide a compact, operations-first playbook for running a field pilot POC with a mid-market enterprise (approx. 50k monthly token volume expected).
- Focus: reliable inference (latency SLOs), telemetry for quality drift, and clear escalation/rollback steps so customer team can exercise production paths without full Dedicated commitment.

Scope & Non-Goals:
- In scope: hosted model variants + optional Dedicated burst capacity, routing policy for fallbacks, KV cache warmup, primary alerting and cost telemetry.
- Out of scope: full security review for on-prem (we'll handoff to Private team if customer requests VPC).

Success criteria (what the customer agrees to):
- End-to-end demo with sample traffic: 95th pct latency < 350ms for short prompts, error rate < 0.3% over 72h test window.
- Regression check on 200 prompt-set evals showing no quality drop > 2% against baseline.
- Instrumentation: token-level cost breakdown and trace for any request exceeding 1s.

Stakeholders & Roles:
- Customer PM: Sarah Li (customer side) — decision maker for acceptance.
- SE Lead (owner): Ava Thompson — overall POC ops and runbook lead.
- Obs/Telemetry SME: Diego Martinez — dashboards, alerts, SLI setup.
- Deployment Engineer: Priya Shah — infra, model pinning, canary steps.
- Solutions SRE: Lucas Nguyen — rollback, runbook, incident lead.

High-level timeline (3-week focused pilot):
- Pre-week (Day -5 to -1): preflight and smoke test
  - Confirm API keys, customer IP allowlist, base dataset of 200 eval prompts.
  - Warm KV cache with synthetic traffic.
  - Baseline perf run and upload traces to dashboard.

- Week 1 (Day 0–7): Controlled integration + initial workshop
  - Day 0: Kickoff + workshop (30–45m) covering SLA targets, routing policies, and fallback behavior.
  - Day 1–3: Integration support (SDK keys, example code). Run 1k synthetic requests, compare latency distribution.
  - Day 4: Instrumentation review: ensure token-cost metric and 95/99 latency traces visible.
  - Day 6–7: Quick evaluation on the 200 prompt set for quality regression.

- Week 2 (Day 8–14): Scale validation + fault-injection
  - Ramp to target QPS in controlled batches. Enable KV cache persistence.
  - Introduce planned failure window (5–10m) to exercise automatic fallback to smaller model variant. Validate no customer-facing errors.
  - Mid-week sync with customer ops to review dashboards and any surprises.

- Week 3 (Day 15–21): Stability window + handoff planning
  - Run 72h stability window at production-like load. Capture traces/recordings for post-mortem.
  - Run acceptance evaluation and prepare final performance/quality report.
  - Handoff session: Recommend next steps (Dedicated reserve, Private package, or production cutover).

Daily/Meeting cadence:
- 15m SE standup (internal) 9:30 PT — quick blockers and status.
- Tri-weekly sync with customer: Day 0, Day 7, Day 14, Day 21 (30–45m).
- On-call rotation for pilot: week-based, primary = Lucas Nguyen, secondary = Priya Shah.

Task tracker (compact):
- Preflight: API allowlist (owner: Priya) — status: done
- Baseline perf run (owner: Diego) — status: done
- Workshop slides + demo notebook (owner: Ava) — status: in_progress
- KV cache warmup script (owner: Priya) — status: done
- Metric dashboard (owner: Diego) — status: in_progress
- Canary rollout policy (owner: Ava) — status: todo
- Failure injection plan (owner: Lucas) — status: todo
- Acceptance eval (owner: Priya & Diego) — status: todo

Primary monitoring & alerting checklist (observability):
- Must-haves to surface within first 24h:
  - 95th and 99th latency (per-model) time series.
  - Token-level cost and per-request cost distribution.
  - Error rate by route and underlying model variant.
  - Trace links for any request > 1s with request payload and model variant.
  - Drop in output-quality score (automated eval) > 1.5% triggers review.

- Alert thresholds (examples):
  - latency_p95 > 600ms for 5m -> P1 page to SE on-call.
  - error_rate > 1% for 10m -> P1 page.
  - cost_per_minute spike +50% -> P2 alert (Ops/finance).
  - eval_quality_drop > 2% on rolling 24h -> P2 and schedule immediate eval run.

Runbook snippets (short):
- If latency_p95 alert fires:
  1) Check model variant utilization and GPU saturation in console.
  2) If saturation, trigger burst to dedicated pool (if enabled) and notify customer.
  3) If not saturation, collect 10 example traces and escalate to runtime team with correlation id.

- If fallback failure observed during canary:
  1) Roll back routing policy to previous stable policy (rollout UI).
  2) If throwable errors persist, throttle new requests and open incident bridge.

Risk register (brief):
- Risk: Initial KV cache cold-start causes high latency spikes. Mitigation: run warmup script 24h prior and keep synthetic traffic during weekend.
- Risk: Customer traffic differs significantly (longer context lengths). Impact: cost and latency. Mitigation: monitor sequence_length distribution and enable auto-quantization profile if variance high.
- Risk: Acceptance eval shows quality regression. Mitigation: revert to pinned baseline model and run root-cause eval with model artifacts.

Customer workshop agenda (Day 0, 45m):
- 5m: Goals and success criteria.
- 10m: Architecture walkthrough: model variants, routing, caches.
- 10m: Observability and what you’ll see in the console.
- 10m: Failure modes and escalation pathways.
- 10m: Q&A + action items.

Deliverables at close of pilot:
- 1-page performance and quality summary (deliverable)
- Dashboard links and retained traces for 30 days
- Runbook + recommended next-step checklist (Dedicated commitment sizing or Private handoff)

Post-mortem triggers (auto):
- Any P1 incident during stability window.
- Failure to meet 2/3 success criteria after remediation attempts.

Notes to SEs (quick tips):
- Bring a prebuilt demo notebook that can be switched between model variants with a single config flag.
- Keep eval prompts anonymized if customer data is sensitive.
- Prioritize visibility: a single broken metric view is worse than missing one detailed metric.

Appendix: quick links and commands
- Baseline perf script: github.com/redwood-inference/pilot-deploy/scripts/baseline.sh
- Dashboard template: Confluence:FieldPilot-Runbook#dash-template
- Incident bridge link (temp): https://zoom.us/j/xxxxxx

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm whether customer wants audit-level tracing (HSM/KMS) — security signoff may add 5 business days.
- Finalize Dedicated burst sizing if customer requires sustained QPS > 2x our hosted cap.

Last edited notes:
- 2025-02-14: Added canary failure steps and updated alert thresholds after runbook dry-run.
- 2025-02-10: Initial draft created.
